text.0_Siman, 0_Paragraph: SIMAN ALEF. TO AWAKEN AT THE MORNING WATCH. As soon as you wake up, say "Mode Ani Lefanecha melech rahum..." and you do not need to wash your hands, and some say that you do need to. (Siddur Hashem of Rabbi Ya`aqov Emden)
text.0_Siman, 1_Paragraph: One must immediately wash his hands properly (according to Jewish law), even if he is not getting up. One should not have a gentile maid, or a Jewess who is a "Nidda", because he can bring on the sitra ahra onto him, and bring bad upon him. (Aharonim)
text.0_Siman, 2_Paragraph: One should dress properly and awake and midnight, and one who does can defeat his bad inclination (ibid.)
text.0_Siman, 3_Paragraph: One may not walk four Amot (cubits) without washed hands, this is a very strict matter. If he has no cup near him, he should walk less then four cubits (amot). (ibid.)  {not like many who rely on the opinion "the whole house is like four cubits"}
text.0_Siman, 4_Paragraph: It is is forbidden to recite blessings (or learn Torah) in front of the water used to do Netilat Yadayim, one should pour it out or cover it. (ibid.)
text.0_Siman, 5_Paragraph: (After Asher Yatzar) Right away he should recite all the morning blessings until "VaAni Abarchem" (The end of Brikat HaTorah) (AriZ"al)
text.0_Siman, 6_Paragraph: (I have said that "Right away recite all the blessings...") And this is after he is already dressed properly, (Because) one should not dress and bless (simultaneously), because one may not do other things while reciting blessings.
text.0_Siman, 7_Paragraph: In the night, one should say Vidui (The repentance prayer) and the Tiqqun Hazot (The midnight rite) according to the formula of the Ari Za"l - and the time of midnight is 12 hours after midday (See Birke Yosef, Siman Alef).
text.0_Siman, 8_Paragraph: (After Tiqqun Hazot,) if one is not able to stay awake until the light of the day, he should sleep, and should not remove his clothing - in order not to enter a doubt wether or not to recite the Birkot HaShahar again (See Birke Yosef, Siman Mem Zayin).
text.0_Siman, 9_Paragraph: There is an obligation for everyone in every place to arise before sunrise (See Mahaziq Beracha, Siman Alef)
text.0_Siman, 10_Paragraph: One is able to drink coffee without sugar before sunrise, and even after sunrise before prayer. (See Birke Yosef, Siman Pe Tet)
text.1_Siman, 0_Paragraph: SIMAN BET. THE LAWS OF SISITH.                                   The required size of the Tallit: It must be large enough to cover the face and body until the chest. (Birke Yosef Siman Tet Zayin)
text.1_Siman, 1_Paragraph: The Tallit Katan is worn on a garment, and is meant to be slept with, and not removed in a bathroom. (Birke Yosef Siman Het)
text.1_Siman, 2_Paragraph: The strings (of the sisit) should always be separated. If they were a little stuck together, one may not separated them on Shabbat. (Gan HaMelech Siman Samech He)
text.1_Siman, 3_Paragraph: When blessing "Lehit'atef B'sisit" with a Sheva under the Bet (B'sisit not Basisit) (Birke Yosef Siman Het).
text.1_Siman, 4_Paragraph: After blessing do the attifa                                         {wrapping the Tallit around the head like an Arab, '''leaving the face uncovered'''', and first wrapping the left corners on the right shoulder, than on top of those corners {still on the right shoulder} put the right corners}.                                                                                                                                             The Aharonim don't rule like the Bet Yaaqob (who rules to cover the face). (Shulhan Aruch Se'if Het)
text.1_Siman, 5_Paragraph: The wrapping of the tallit takes place standing.
text.1_Siman, 6_Paragraph: There is an obligation on everyone to look at the sisit strings and to imagine he is wearing it with techelet (a blue string). (Birke Yosef Siman Het)
text.1_Siman, 7_Paragraph: On the topic of covering the head with the Tallit, it is clear and obvious, that when saying the blessing he must wrap his head like an Arab (as said above) for the time it takes to walk four amot (about two seconds), and afterward, he can wear it according to his minhag. (Mahaziq Berach Siman Het)
text.1_Siman, 8_Paragraph: The holes [in the corners of the garment] that hold the sisit, may not be more than three finger breadths [about the size of an adults thumb-nail] away from the edges of the corner. (See Mahaziq Bracha Siman Yud Alef)
text.1_Siman, 9_Paragraph: One entire string that rips off deems the whole invalid. And if a string rips off [not entirely, but-] at the knot near the whole, deems it invalid. (ibid. Siman Yud Bet)
text.1_Siman, 10_Paragraph: One who didn't have sisit or tefillin, [and finds some] in the middle of pesuqe deZimra, may make a blessing in the middle of the psalms. (see Birke Yosef Siman Nun Gimel).         But not at the end of pesuqe diZimra before Yishtabach, but rather (he should wait till after barechu) between Yishtabach and the Beracha Yosser Or. (Shulhan Aruch ibid.)
text.1_Siman, 11_Paragraph: One who sleeps with his tallit at night isn't required to make another blessing in the morning (Acharonim in siman Het)                                                                     {Although the Shulhan Aruch rules to make a blessing, it is a case of Safeq berachot (a doubt whether or not to say a blessing), and maybe even a Safeq Safeq Safeqah (triple doubt), and we can apply the ruling "Safeq Berachot LeHaQel, afilu neghed Maran" - We rule lenient (not to recite) blessings (in a time of doubt) , even if it is not like the opinion of Maran (the Shulhan Aruch)}
text.1_Siman, 12_Paragraph: One may not drag the sisit strings on the floor, and if the tallit is too long, he should take the two back sisiyot and tuck it into his belt. (Birke Yosef Siman Kaf Alef)
text.2_Siman, 0_Paragraph: SIMAN GIMMEL. LAWS OF TEFILLIN.:                            He dons in the Tallit Gadol, and afterwards, he dons Tefillin, and this is even though he has a Tallit Qattan already on him always. (Birke Yosef Siman Kaf He)
text.2_Siman, 1_Paragraph: When walking on his way (to synagogue) a man should be careful to wear Tefillin, both the hand Tefillin and the head Tefillin, and not to be negligent this great and strict Missva because of mockery from others, and from this he he''l be humble in all his ways. Many people only put shel yad Siman Kaf Vav
text.2_Siman, 2_Paragraph: If one forgets and puts on the Tefila Shel Rosh before the Shel Yad, one doesn't need to remove it, rather he should put on the Tefila Shel Yad then, (without removing the Shel Rosh first). Shiurei Beracha ibid.
text.2_Siman, 3_Paragraph: One should be careful when putting away the Tefillin to put the Shel Rosh and then the Shel Yad (should be in front of the Shel Rosh) in order to take out the Shel Yad from muscle memory (not to by mistake take out the Shel Rosh first). It is even more correct to make the Tefillin pouch wide (and instead of putting the Shel Yad in front of the Shel Rosh) to put it side by side, (but to still make sure that) the Shel Yad should be in the side which the right hand is accustomed to reach for {for example: if one's right hand normally reaches for the left side of the bag, he should put the Shel Yad on the left}. (Birke Yosef Siman Kaf Het)
text.2_Siman, 4_Paragraph: (The correct sequence is:) to put the Tefillin on the bicep in the correct place, then to bless the blessing (leHaniach Tefillin) and only then, to tighten the knot on hid arm (Shulhan Aruch Siman Kaf He)
text.2_Siman, 5_Paragraph: It is forbidden to interrupt [With speach] between putting on the Shel Yad and putting on the Shel Rosh. If one does interrupt, he must also make a blessing on the Shel Rosh "`Al Misswath Tefillin". (ibid.)      {and not like the Ashkenazim who always make a blessing on the Shel Rosh.
text.2_Siman, 6_Paragraph: After tightening the Shel Yad (onto his arm), he must (wrap the strap around the box in order to) tie the "Yud" knot with the box, and after that he must continue and wrap the strap on the arms (seven or eight times depending on the custom), but one may not wrap the strap even once on the bicep,          {unlike many Sepharadim and Ashkenazim who wrap once one the arm before wrapping on the forearm once, and surely not like those "Hasidim" who wrap three or six times before wrapping on the forearm, to make a Shin}
text.2_Siman, 7_Paragraph: After wrapping seven times on the arm        {or eight, depending the custom, [whether or not to count the first wrap as a real wrap, since it is only a half wrap]}      he must place the Shel Rosh (Birke Yosef ibid.)     {And not like those who wrap first on the hand, then put the Shel Rosh, then unwrap the hand, and then wrap the finger and etc.}
text.2_Siman, 8_Paragraph: One may not take out the Shel Rosh from the pouch before putting on the Shel Yad. (Shulhan Arukh ibid.)
text.2_Siman, 10_Paragraph: The black pain on the straps must be on the outside, and may not be reverse. (See Shulchan Aruch Siman Zayin Chaf). And there are those who write one to put black on both sides.
text.2_Siman, 11_Paragraph: When putting on the Tefillin Shel Yad, the custom (for Sefardim) is to cover the arm with the Tallit (and to wrap under the Tallit were no one can see). The law is (according to Kabbala) that one must cover the Tefillin Shel Rosh with the Tallit (for the entirety of the time of wearing the Tefillin). (see Birke Yosef ibid.)
text.2_Siman, 12_Paragraph: One should be careful that the "Yud" of the knot (of the Shel Yad) should not separate from the box. (Shulchan Aruch ibid.) And it should never separate even when it is in the bag, (and one is not wearing it). This is the opinion of Mahary''y Semah.
text.2_Siman, 13_Paragraph: (The custom is to) wrap the Shel Yad sitting, the Shel Rosh standing, and to wrap the strap around the middle finger three times, once on the top joint, and twice on the second joint (to form the shape of a Shin). This is the opinion of the Ari Z''l.
text.2_Siman, 14_Paragraph: If one interrupts between donning the Shel Yad and Shel Rosh ---To answer Amen--- ----After the fact---- he doesn't need to bless on the Shel Rosh. (Aharonim)
text.2_Siman, 15_Paragraph: One who errs and blesses on the Shel Yad "`Al Misvat Tefillin", fulfills his obligation. (Mahaziq Beracha Siman Kaf He. And one can chec there for the laws regarding an Ashkenazi).
text.2_Siman, 16_Paragraph: One may not remove his intention from the fact that he is wearing Tefillin. And it is better not to remove his intention even while learning Torah and praying the 'Amidah, and one must be very careful, for the punishment is very great. (Mahaziq Beracha Siman Kaf Het)
text.2_Siman, 17_Paragraph: (If one was wearing tefillin and it comes) past sunset, one should remove it immediately, (See Birke Yosef Siman Lamed)
text.2_Siman, 18_Paragraph: (If one erred before Shaharit) and blessed on the Tefillin at night, or thought it was day and it was still night, he doesn't need to repeat the blessing after it becomes morning. (ibid.)
text.2_Siman, 19_Paragraph: The opinion of the Zohar and the Ari is that wearing Tefillin Shel Rabenu Tam is also an obligation, and that it isn't G-d forbid because of doubt whether the opinion of Rashi or Rabenu Tam is correct.
text.2_Siman, 20_Paragraph: (Maran rules in the Shulhan Aruch, that one may not wear Rabbeinu Tam Tefillin unless he is known by the people for his piety, but this is only because of the issue of him looking haughty in front of everyone, therefore,) if it is common practice of people in one's city, to were Rabbeinu Tam Tefillin together with Rashi, ones SHOULD were both pairs, and (this is the ruling because) there is no haughtiness here.
text.2_Siman, 21_Paragraph: If possible, it is better to cover (the Rabbeinu Tam Tefillin) with a hat (under the Tallit which is already on his Tefillin as mentioned above)
text.2_Siman, 22_Paragraph: (If one doesn't live in such a city {as mentioned above} and is therefore not accustomed to were them together, but rather) if he is accustomed to praying with Rashi Tefillin, and to remove them after prayers, and don Rabeinu Tam Tefillin, (in order that people can't tell its Rabbeinu Tam, such a person) does not say a blessing on Tefillin.
text.2_Siman, 23_Paragraph: (If one unintentionally) donned Rabbeinu Tam, thinking it was Rashi Tefillin, and prayed with them, and after removing them, he saw that it was Rabbeinu Tam, he puts on Rashi Tefillin - and blesses on them.
text.2_Siman, 24_Paragraph: (And if one puts on Rabbeinu Tam after Tefilla, as said above), although he doesn't bless on them, he still may not talk in between donning the Shel Yad and the Shel Rosh.
text.2_Siman, 25_Paragraph: And the correct practice is to wear both Tefillin for Shaharit, and this what is -required- (according to Qabbalah)
text.2_Siman, 26_Paragraph: (One who is accustomed to also don Tefillin) at Minha, only dons Tefillin Rabbeinu Tam.
text.2_Siman, 27_Paragraph: (And one who is accustomed to also don Tefillin at Minha,) one Ereb Shabbat, he may not don Tefillin.
text.2_Siman, 28_Paragraph: On Minha on Rosh Hodesh, he -may- don Tefillin, (even though he may not learn Torah with Tefillin)
text.2_Siman, 29_Paragraph: On Rosh Hodesh, one may not remove the Tefillin until Qaddish after bringing the Torah to the Hechal (From Ot Kaf, until here, we see in Hayyim Sha'al siman Alef.)
text.2_Siman, 30_Paragraph: One may not have any interposition between the Tefilllin and his skin, and in Shealot Uteshuvot Pene Ari Hadash, literally in siman vav, it is written that white dust that is in interposition, since it is not visible, it isn't an interposition, and I have written, that one may answer from what I have written in Birke Yosef Siman Kaf Zayin, that even something that isn't an interposition, one should be strict, and check it as if it was literally th Bigde Kehuna, and on this one must do a lot of research.
